title: Enjoying the update
content:
I too was originally skeptical of being forced into their sync system.  I read their terms of service and frankly some of the language was frightening, but I had a couple email exchanges with their extremely responsive customer service and I was satisfied they could not use my private entries in the future.  I've been using for two months now and their sync service is fantastic.  I had period issues with iCloud with Day One Classic, but I've never had an issue so far syncing between my iMac, iPhone, and iPad.  

The bottom line is that for YEARS I struggled to consistently journal - since getting Dayone in 2012, and now Dayone 2 - I journal more than I have in my entire life.  It is awesome for capturing moments and recording my life.  I know some day there won't be a price you can put on having these entries.  It's so easy to capture photos in DayOne 2 and being able to have multiple photos in an entry is awesome.  

If your nervous about their sync, just read the news, it's a risk we all take using the cloud, but to me the trade off is that I'm building a lifetime of memories with this app.

Update MANY years later - I wrote the above a long time ago. I’ve been using this app daily and haven’t missed a day since 2015. The new conversation element is amazing to me. It helps me journal throughout the day more instead of trying to remember the whole day. Quite frankly the AI asks some very insightful questions that help me go deeper and have really improved my entries. I’m hoping eventually they will add the ability to use AI to “converse” with your older entires like “hey how did I handle this previously . . . “.

UPDATE 6/11/2026 - after giving original plus members (I’ve been using the journal since 2012) the daily chat for about the last 8 months the tiers changed with no notice or warning.  Went to use it today and see now I’m “silver” and have to upgrade to use it. I get it, apps need to make money but it’s a shame is the same old methods - hook you on the service for some indefinite period of time then take it away.  Not a lot of loyalty for long time subscribers.  I feel like that is disappointing. Even changing the tiers and not keeping it the same. Might be time to look for other options or use apples.

Really a shame they just don’t have as much loyalty toward their subscribers and users that have been here since well Day One.  Pun intended.  Their latest bait and switch on features I just thought was a really poor thing to do. Gave the use of chat for like 8 months then raised the price of the tier I was on and decided to take away the features.  I was using the chat in beta. Very disappointed and a little sad to have to login for another option.

I read their terms of service and frankly some of the language was frightening, but I had a couple email exchanges with their extremely responsive customer service and I was satisfied they could not use my private entries in the future.  I've been using for two months now and their sync service is fantastic.  I had period issues with iCloud with Day One Classic, but I've never had an issue so far syncing between my iMac, iPhone, and iPad.  

The bottom line is that for YEARS I struggled to consistently journal - since getting Dayone in 2012, and now Dayone 2 - I journal more than I have in my entire life.  It is awesome for capturing moments and recording my life.  I know some day there won't be a price you can put on having these entries.  It's so easy to capture photos in DayOne 2 and being able to have multiple photos in an entry is awesome.  

If your nervous about their sync, just read the news, it's a risk we all take using the cloud, but to me the trade off is that I'm building a lifetime of memories with this app.

Update MANY years later - I wrote the above a long time ago. I’ve been using this app daily and haven’t missed a day since 2015. The new conversation element is amazing to me. It helps me journal throughout the day more instead of trying to remember the whole day. Quite frankly the AI asks some very insightful questions that help me go deeper and have really improved my entries. I’m hoping eventually they will add the ability to use AI to “converse” with your older entires like “hey how did I handle this previously . . . “.

UPDATE 6/11/2026 - after giving original plus members (I’ve been using the journal since 2012) the daily chat for about the last 8 months the tiers changed with no notice or warning.  Went to use it today and see now I’m “silver” and have to upgrade to use it. I get it, apps need to make money but it’s a shame is the same old methods - hook you on the service for some indefinite period of time then take it away.  Not a lot of loyalty for long time subscribers.  I feel like that is disappointing. Even changing the tiers and not keeping it the same. Might be time to look for other options or use apples.

Really a shame they just don’t have as much loyalty toward their subscribers and users that have been here since well Day One.  Pun intended.  Their latest bait and switch on features I just thought was a really poor thing to do. Gave the use of chat for like 8 months then raised the price of the tier I was on and decided to take away the features.  I was using the chat in beta. Very disappointed and a little sad to have to login for another option.

title: A staple for more than a dozen years, but I’m getting wary and looking around
content:
I use this app probably more than any app I’ve ever purchased besides 2Do. It’s a page-one-on-my-homescreen staple. 

But I’m side-eyeing the direction it’s going in, starting with the needlessly clumsy interface overhaul that turned viewing On This Day (probably my favorite feature) from one tap to multiple taps that are so unintuitive that more than a year later I still stumble over the order. I’ve got the OTD widget, which ostensibly should cancel out that problem, but half the time I tap on it, it opens the app, jumps to OTD and then immediately jumps out of it, negating the whole purpose. 

And now it’s adding a new tier and more upsells for things I absolutely do not want. I realize every developer has to look like it embraces AI even though people vocally cannot stand this stuff but I do not need a chat bot in my journal. I wonder if anybody does, especially for $75 a year.

I assume the feature bloat, interface musical chairs and upsells (and bugs — currently dealing with an obnoxious one that re-downloads and re-adds a photo whenever I move it around an entry) will continue and increase, and while I have a lot of time invested into this journal, I’ve always kept that data in other formats in case it all goes south. That day isn’t here yet, but I’m looking around at the competition for the first time since I purchased Day One years ago.

title: A staple for more than a dozen years, but I’m getting wary and looking around
content:
I use this app probably more than any app I’ve ever purchased besides 2Do. It’s a page-one-on-my-homescreen staple. 

But I’m side-eyeing the direction it’s going in, starting with the needlessly clumsy interface overhaul that turned viewing On This Day (probably my favorite feature) from one tap to multiple taps that are so unintuitive that more than a year later I still stumble over the order. I’ve got the OTD widget, which ostensibly should cancel out that problem, but half the time I tap on it, it opens the app, jumps to OTD and then immediately jumps out of it, negating the whole purpose. 

And now it’s adding a new tier and more upsells for things I absolutely do not want. I realize every developer has to look like it embraces AI even though people vocally cannot stand this stuff but I do not need a chat bot in my journal. I wonder if anybody does, especially for $75 a year.

I assume the feature bloat, interface musical chairs and upsells (and bugs — currently dealing with an obnoxious one that re-downloads and re-adds a photo whenever I move it around an entry) will continue and increase, and while I have a lot of time invested into this journal, I’ve always kept that data in other formats in case it all goes south. That day isn’t here yet, but I’m looking around at the competition for the first time since I purchased Day One years ago.

title: all the little things
content:
a review of a journaling app, i suppose, is as good a place to reminisce as any.

here goes.

i miss when software, especially that on iOS, reflected a virtually irrepressible care and concern for “the little things,” those little flourishes of care that distinguish mere utilities for “getting the job done” from little extensions of self that bring joy upon use.

it breaks my heart to say that recent interface changes have downgraded this app from the latter to, tragically, the former.

to elude this peculiar “update” to a paradoxically downgraded experience, i kept my Day One on version 2023.23 until upgrading to iOS 26 broke its share sheet, forcing me to update Day One to the current version.

for perspective, i’ve been using Day One as an offline (multi-)journal for the greater part of a decade, and haven’t found much (personal) use for syncing, though i know it’s a wonderful feature for those choosing to use it.

this offline only use in mind, consider how horrendous the UX is to not only have to select “skip for now”—a “for now” that inspires concern that One Day, this “for now” will give way to a mandatory “or else,” or no-entry scenario otherwise—on a full-height prompt wall with no dismiss button and a picture of someone i don’t know (as opposed to a settings specified picture from a journal entry), temporarily rendering the better title for the app: “Day One Promptwall: Private, yet Curiously Inaccessible Diary.” *then* i must dismiss a “Not Now/Sign In” banner to atop all of entries, which robs me of screen height should i not dismiss.

but perhaps more egregious than either of these, there is now an always present, un-collapsing “Sign In” button that…
takes precedence over *the name of the current journal*. this is insane to me: the current journal’s name will literally be truncated by ellipsis to… make way for a collection of letters vastly more important, “Sign In.” and why, when this very same (read: redundant, in terms of UI) “feature” can be accessed simply by tapping another button a few pixels to the right? could it at least be hidden if the user taps “Not Now” in the “Don’t lose your data” banner?

wow.

and there is no “opt out,” “manage without sync,” “let iCloud backups handle it,” or even “use offline.” it’s only, “you’re literally insane for not uploading all of your most personal inner thoughts to the computers of people you’ve never met, so it’s comically obtrusive full-heights, banners, and ellipses for you!”

beyond this, Day One circa 2023 had nifty little journal stats and streak data atop the journal, and while i know one can still access this information elsewhere, it was nice to have it immediately present and prominent. now, in their place are tabs that by Liquid Glass’ design language should probably be moved to where the “Journals, Prompts, More” buttons currently are on iOS 26. (an incidentally welcome change, i’d think, at least it is in brainscape.)

if “Lists, Calendar, Media, Map” were made to be the Liquid Glass button cluster on the bottom, the “Journals” button currently there would be unnecessary, and the “Prompts” button could be rolled into a long-press feature of the “+” button—which curiously is not vertically aligned with the other button buttons? 🤔 (i think it would be nice in general to have a little more Liquid Glass style, such as collapsing the top bar to one word, “[Current Journal],” when scrolling upward and allowing timeline content to still be visible even as it scrolls past the clock and iOS connectivity indicators toward infinity beyond the top of the device).

next, in the timeline, there is so. much. dead space: each entry is now a massively juicy, septuple-height chonk. it’s like helplessly wandering through a visual desert interspersed with oases of memories. i know some people like that, and i don’t mind that they do, but i wish there were a setting for a little more of a compact presentation per entry. maybe one where the attached image (glyphed with a “+” if more than one) lies right-justified and frosted for readability just beneath the entry title and words. something modern like that.

speaking of which, the timeline no longer displays attached photos as right justified by default, so in journal entries without words, photos and media now leap to the far left in timeline view, so that the relative locations of photos in the timeline look awkwardly haphazard and inconsistent, slapdash even, when scrolling through memories.

also, long pressing an entry in the timeline does not provide an option to copy or move it to another journal. but it never did, so that’s just a wish listing.

nor does it have an option to display entry information/copy x-callback url (now THIS is a nitpick, but you’d be surprised how useful it is to directly link to a specific entry from another app. if you haven’t yet, please try it!) another wish listing 😊 

oh! here’s a little thing, the 2023ish version color coded the journal titles in the share sheet selector, now they’re all white and indistinguishable, other than by their letters.

also regarding formatting, the entries themselves don’t even have as much formatting versatility as Apple Notes (?!), eg they have only one (?!) highlighting color. it wouldn’t hurt to have more formatting niceties as well, like super/subscript, easier drag and drop of text/images, text beside images, etc.

and perhaps most of all, if you make any of these changes, please consider making them for everyone. i understand locking things behind subwalls for money, but the rest of us (or even the Plus’ers like myself) shouldn’t be abandoned to UX friction. i know ⌛️💸 is the official emoji combo of all apps these days, but please have mercy.

title: Half Liquid Glass, Half iOS 18
content:
December 2025:
I’ve used Day One for ages now (over a decade?) and it’s been a great experience.

However it needs further updated with Liquid Glass and other design elements in iOS 26.

I’m glad the keyboard is there as that’s one of my favorite redesigns, and something about it feels slightly more useful/functional than iOS 18. The new lower bar/selector is there, and the Journals pop-up menu is super nice (though why isn’t the half-sized menu translucent like in Maps), but that bar is about it.

The handy Plus button for creating an entry is just asking for Liquid Glass, instead of that old iOS 18 flat style. Things already updated their Plus button. It’s a very minor detail, yet it’s an object that’s always seen.

And what’s bothering me the most is the headers, inside entries themselves and when scrolling through journal entries. The headers are too “hard” and large and obtuse, a relic of iOS 18. They need to adopt the tinted and blurred headers for iOS 26, or something very similar that honors the journal’s color. Entries will look amazing with that new UI ambiance. For inspiration, simply look at Apple Journal.

The text modifier bar that shows above the keyboard when entering text also could be updated to be more similar to Apple Notes. People whine that no real new features were provided with iOS 26 or that the redesign is useless, but this dynamic bar in Notes has been superbly useful. I use Notes everyday and it’s so much better than in iOS 18, in a way that I didn’t even know I needed. iOS 18 Notes was fine, but iOS 26 Notes is smart. Day One could use a smart text entry bar, instead of hiding all the main text options in the Aa menu.

Also, seeing my old review from years ago, I don’t believe Day One updated the Watch app to be able to view entries. This makes no sense, and in light of now having Apple Notes on my Watch, is perhaps unacceptable.

I ditched Evernote years ago due to the nonsense the new owner pulled, replacing it with Anytype.

I’ve eyed the Apple Journals app a lot… Something about it calls to me. It’s so elegant with its iOS 26 implementation and feels inviting. I’m not sure it’s feasible for me to switch from Day One to Journal (with a couple thousand entries in multiple journals and no import function in Journal), and I’m not sure I even want to do that — but basically I wish I were writing my entries in the Journal interface right now. Because it’s fully up to date in design, and Day One is not. I don’t think you’ve half-assed it, but it does feel half done, half undone.

I also love Journal’s main screen dashboard so much, with the Insights and Places. Day One has its version in the More tab, but I’m sort of wondering why it’s been relegated to third class citizen as the third button. I can envision a nice welcome/dashboard screen in Day One being first, with a plus button to rapidly make an entry, instead of the first view being the scroll of entries. Like, why is the Streaks overview hidden down at the bottom of the third tab?

Speaking of entries, I also love Journal’s way of depicting entries with photos in the scroll view; Journal handles this in a more inviting way by making them large, and the entries are rounded instead of Day One’s arcane hard edges. I feel like Day One could have two view options, the current email-style list and one which is more dynamic with the content inside, when it includes photos or whatever. 

Journal also highlights music for example, and I’m not sure Day One can even present a song as an object insofar as I’ve seen; it’s only possible to add it to the entry metadata, tucked far away in the Entry Info menu… Really? Day One should handle media more dynamically and more elegantly. The current implementation is a very old style of iOS/app design, where apps were just a screen with a simple header and only text as the content. But we’ve come a long way since that.

I don’t need Day One to lose its identity and look just like Journal. But I absolutely want Day One updated to iOS 26 UI/UX standards and sensitivities. There’s a trend of first party apps looking and feeling better, especially with iOS 26’s massive changes in design. And similarly there’s a toxic trend of third party apps resisting new iOS ideas, wherein I develop frustration and impatience when my most used third party apps can’t be bothered to get with the times, times which I quite enjoy and which are here to stay and are going to evolve along this trajectory, no matter who dislikes it. 

I understand Day One may still be working to implement changes in a way that honors its own branding and style, but if a year goes by and iOS 18 elements are still lingering around, well that starts to make an app feel anti-Apple, and I didn’t buy into the Apple ecosystem to utilize apps which exploit my usage and money only to resist the environment they’re benefiting from. And there are a handful od party apps like this, particularly Bearable’s utterly obnoxious proprietary design and behaviors (and lack of basic iOS functions like Search/highlight). If you want to see design done bad on iOS, in a way that pretends to look good until you use it and realize how odd it is (not even mentioning the bugs they always have), just to try Bearable.

For a third party app that does its own design right while honoring iOS sensitivities, look at Things. May all third party apps who don’t want to look like a first party app look to Things for inspiration.

I just don’t want Day One to become a relic. It lived through iOS 7 I believe, and I very much look forward to it not just living through iOS 26, but thriving in design, implantation, and overall UX/ambiance.

Day One is where we spend time with our most personal contemplations. It should be a modern and elegant space. I think if you commit to it, Day One can be way nicer than Journal, not just in having more features, but in elegance and ambiance.

The only thing better is printed material and external flash drives passed down. (Doing that too. And oh, Day One exports to a printed book feature at a cost, or free pdf)

Once you play with it, you’ll want to upgrade to paid.

This may revolutionize your life.

title: The power of journaling!
content:
I’ve been using DayOne as my private journal for over 6 years.  I started using it when I realized I was never doing the journaling I wanted to do because 1.) writing on paper meant leaving it around the house for prying eyes, and 2.) I never had my journal on me when I had something to say.  Keeping my journal with its own password on my phone means I can jot down my thoughts anywhere - in the bathroom (honestly, the most common place when I started), sitting next to whomever I was ranting about, sitting in the doctor’s office before a procedure, in the car waiting for someone, etc.

I have had multiple journaling templates over the years that provide a little guidance to my morning journaling - it is a place to collect data from my habits, build new practices into daily life, and the place that I process through my thoughts & feelings.  It helps me keep in mind the insights I’ve gained on prior morning contemplations. 

I have a template for our weekly food plan - it has some always-scheduled meals (Taco Tuesday with the list of items) plus a list of favorite easy meals to pick from for Wednesday and Thursday nights (always a challenge!). It now takes me 5 minutes to figure out what we will eat for the week and another 5 minutes to make my shopping list. 

I have another journaling prompt that walks me through intention-setting before an event or trip - this has transformed vacations so I can relax into the activities and feelings that I want to have instead of just reacting to everyone else. 

I have a file for recipes and food ideas, too.  

DayOne is an integral part of my life now.  I recommend it to friends, family, and my patients.  Thank you!!

title: Fallen behind other apps with more features
content:
I’ve been using Day One since the beginning. They have fallen behind some other journaling apps with more customizable template options such as formatting tables without using Markdown and show no sign of motivation to add these features. Instead they’re focusing on adding fluff—things that take little development effort, like more journaling prompts. This allows them to show they’re regularly updating the app, though it doesn’t address missing features. Eventually they’ll lose people over those missing features like more customizable formatting. 

Rather than easy formatting of posts, you have to use Markdown. And now, without any apparent notification to their users—users who used Markdown as Day One’s only way to create a table in an entry—they no longer even support printing of tables made with Markdown. 

I’m starting to think that Day One just doesn’t have good enough developers who can make significant improvements to their app. I’m about to not renew my Premium membership, and I’m looking at their competitors who are offering more features, too. 

Day One, get it together and make some significant changes your users want or you’ll lose longtime users (as well as prospective users) to your competitors. You’ve been riding on your early success far too long. Also, the price of Premium for Plus users should not be the same as for those who are just starting with your app. You literally wouldn’t exist if it weren’t for your Plus users who were there when nobody knew who you were.

title: Best Journal Ever!!
content:
For the first time since I started trying to journal, I’ve been actually consistent with using this app everyday!! I like that when I’m on WiFi it records exactly where I am as I make my entry (anywhere in the world and it even records the time zone correctly). I also really like that if I have to record an entry after the fact, as long as I can remember the correct time I was there, it still (for the most part) records my location correctly. And there’s a feature where you can actually view the entries you’ve recorded on a map (regular or satellite). I can highlight text, bold, italicize, and now even underline while writing. And I can even draw on the page!! Having the ability to tag your entries also allows you to categorize and find them more easily. Now, the last thing I’m waiting for is the ability to change the colors of my highlights to something other than yellow (my choice of course) and to be able to change the color of certain passages of text in my longer entries to make it stand out when I’m searching for it (for instance if I wanted to quickly identify a particular quote). I can also keep up with my favorite photos and videos in here and even add other kinds of attachments. I can record an entry using my voice and finally what I’ve been waiting on for what seems like forever!!! I can attach an audio file of my own! I have voicemail messages I’ve saved from important people in my life who have now passed on and after saving them as .mp3 and placing them in my Files folder on my iPhone/iPad, I can now attach them to an entry and keep the memory forever! Yay, Bloom Built Inc!! You’ve accomplished something I’ve been waiting for all my life!
